Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 72, verse 1:

قل اوحی ........................ احد

The words nafar (group) and rahat (company) apply to any number from three to nine, and it is related that the jinn in this incident were nine. The manner in which the account of this event is begun here shows that the event occurred as follows: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the Qur'an, the jinn listened to the Qur'an, and then they went to their people and conveyed the message. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had no knowledge of this. Allah informed the Messenger (ﷺ) of this entire event through revelation. This was the first such event, and after it there may have been many other occasions on which the Messenger (ﷺ) recited the Qur'an and the jinn listened. This is also indicated by the ahadith related concerning the Messenger's (ﷺ) recitation, in which he recited knowing that the jinn were listening.

Imam Tirmidhi related from Hadrat Jabir ibn Abdullah: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out and recited Surah al-Rahman to his companions, from beginning to end, and all of them fell silent. He (ﷺ) said: 'I recited this surah to the jinn, and they gave a better response to it than you did. Whenever I recited the verse, "So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?" they would say: "None of Your favours, our Lord, do we deny, so to You belongs all praise."'" This narration supports the narration of Ibn Mas'ud which we mentioned earlier.

This is the first occasion in which the hearing of the Qur'an by the jinn is mentioned. Concerning this same occasion, the verses of Surah al-Ahqaf also speak:

وَإِذْ صَرَفْنَا إِلَيْكَ نَفَرًا مِّنَ الْجِنِّ يَسْتَمِعُونَ الْقُرْآنَ ۖ فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوهُ قَالُوا أَنصِتُوا ۖ فَلَمَّا قُضِيَ وَلَّوْا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِم مُّنذِرِينَ ﴿٢�9﴾ قَالُوا يَا قَوْمَنَا إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا كِتَابًا أُنزِلَ مِن بَعْدِ مُوسَىٰ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ وَإِلَىٰ طَرِيقٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ ﴿٣0﴾ يَا قَوْمَنَا أَجِيبُوا دَاعِيَ اللَّهِ وَآمِنُوا بِهِ يَغْفِرْ لَكُم مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمْ وَيُجِركُم مِّنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ ﴿٣1﴾ وَمَن لَّا يُجِبْ دَاعِيَ اللَّهِ فَلَيْسَ بِمُعْجِزٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَيْسَ لَهُ مِن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءُ ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُّبِينٍ ﴿٣2﴾

(And when We turned towards you a group of jinn, listening to the Qur'an. When they were present, they said, "Be silent." When it was concluded, they returned to their people as warners. They said, "O our people, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path. O our people, respond to the caller of Allah and believe in him; He will forgive you your sins and protect you from a painful punishment. And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah will not escape on earth, and he will have no protectors besides Him. Those are in manifest error.")

إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا قُرْآنًا عَجَبًا ﴿١﴾ (We have heard a wondrous Qur'an.)

The first characteristic of the Qur'an that the jinn found evident was that it is wondrous and unfamiliar, and upon hearing it, fear arises in the hearts. Whoever recites or listens to the Qur'an with a sensitive perception and an open heart, with a expansive heart and a balanced taste, will be overwhelmed by it and will find it to be a wondrous thing. It has within it the power of argument, it has immense attractiveness, and its effects are so intense that it produces a powerful vibration and melody in the strings of the heart and conscience. It is wondrous in practice as well; the reaction of the jinn to it is evidence, for they found it thus and immediately became ready to act upon it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 72, verse 2:

"Yahdi ilal rushd" (27:2): "who guides to right conduct." This is the second distinguishing and self-evident quality of the Qur'an, and the group of jinn perceived it at first glance. When they found the reality of the Qur'an within their own hearts, they understood that this is a Book of guidance. Then, instead of the word hidayah (guidance), they used the word irshad, which has a broader meaning than hidayah. That is, this Book guides and shows the path of truth and righteousness. The word rushd also carries another meaning, namely seriousness, moderation, and knowledge and recognition. Thus, this Book guides to the path of rightness with knowledge, recognition, seriousness and moderation, and its manner is scholarly. Through its study, one acquires the faculty of reaching these realities. These results are, as it were, the inherent effects and outcomes of this Book.

The Qur'an is a fountain of rushd and guidance, in that it creates feeling and expansiveness in hearts, and produces the impulse of comprehension and recognition. It creates a connection with Allah, who is the source of the light of guidance. Then this Book joins man with the laws of nature operating throughout this entire universe, and then in practical life this Book proposes a practical system of life. And as a result of this system, humanity attains that elevation which it never attains in any other system. And this Book then brings into being a distinguished civilization and culture, among whose inhabitants the people are extremely distinguished and advanced in intellectual, conceptual, moral, legal and practical respects.

"Fa amanna bihi" (27:2): "So we have believed in it." After hearing the Qur'an, it is a natural and innate reaction that a person accepts it, understands it, and receives a genuine impression from it. Allah, the Exalted, relates this remark of the jinn to admonish the polytheists of Makkah for their lack of learning: you have been listening to the Qur'an for a long time and yet you do not accept it. And you attribute this Book to the jinn; sometimes you say it is a soothsayer's utterance, sometimes you say it is poetry, and sometimes you say he is possessed. And all three had a connection with the jinn. But just look at the condition of the jinn: they were overwhelmed upon hearing the Qur'an, they understood it, and they went out among their people carrying this call. They did not delay even for a moment. They could not restrain themselves; they immediately departed carrying this call and impression. They recognised the truth, accepted it, believed in it, and proclaimed their faith. And they did not practise deceit, nor harbour malice and enmity as the polytheists of Makkah were doing.

"Wa lan ... ahada" (72:2): "And we will never associate anyone with our Lord." This is pure, explicit and sound faith; it contains neither shirk, nor any admixture of illusion, nor any room for superstition. This faith has arisen as a result of comprehending the reality of the Qur'an, and has come into existence as a consequence of the reality to which the Qur'an calls. That is, pure tawhid without any trace of shirk.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 72, verse 3:

﴿And that exalted is the majesty of our Lord; He has not taken a wife nor a son.﴾ (72:3)

Al-Jadd (the root meaning) refers to a portion and share, that is, rank and standing, greatness and dominion. All of these meanings are contained in the word "jadd" and are its reflections. But the general sense is that Allah is of very lofty rank. He is very great and exalted in dignity. Therefore He has taken neither a wife nor a son.

Among the Arabs there was the false notion that the angels are Allah's daughters, and that these daughters came into being in such a way that Allah's wife was a jinn. The jinn themselves, through their own words, refuted this story and fable, declaring that Allah is pure and free from such things. With great disapproval they negated the false attribution to Him, saying that there is no such kinship and that Allah has not taken a son. This is, in effect, a great insult to Allah. All such notions, and those resembling them, are false and polytheistic, whatever form they may take: whether they are polytheistic tales, or the fables of the "aqanim" (hypostases), or any other form.

And indeed, ﴿some foolish ones among us used to speak outrageous lies about Allah﴾ (72:4), and ﴿we had thought that neither humans nor jinn would ever utter a lie against Allah﴾ (72:5).

The jinn are repeating that some of their foolish people held views about Allah that were contrary to the truth, and believed that Allah had a wife and children. After hearing the Qur'an, it became clear to them that these beliefs were not correct, and that those among the jinn who held them were very ignorant and foolish. They were so ignorant that they imagined no human or jinn could ever fabricate a lie against Allah. They believed that no one could invent a falsehood about Allah. Therefore, when some fools adopted the belief that Allah had a wife and children, they accepted it as well, because they thought that no one could possibly attribute a false claim to Allah. Yet this very awareness became the cause of their faith, because their hearts contained pure thought. As soon as someone fabricated a lie against Allah, Allah did not seize him; and as soon as the jinn received the truth, they shook off the dust of misguidance. They found the reality, tasted the true reality, and they spoke out:

﴿Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an that guides to the right path, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord﴾ (72:1-2), and ﴿exalted is the majesty of our Lord; He has taken neither a wife nor a son﴾ (72:3).

This clearing away and purification was granted to them because they reached the truth. This reality was worthy of being considered by the chieftains of Quraysh (Kubara-e-Quraysh), most of whom were arrogant and self-deluded, and who believed that Allah had a wife and daughters. Through this reality, fear of God and caution would have arisen in their hearts, and they would have tried to understand the message that Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ) was presenting before them. The foolish beliefs of the chieftains of Quraysh would have been subjected to doubt regarding their validity, but, alas, this did not happen. The purpose of bringing this story here was also to refute the beliefs of the chieftains of Quraysh. Between the Qur'an and the chieftains of Quraysh there was an ideological war, and this Surah was an example of one of its skirmishes. This Surah was in fact providing a lasting cure for the diseases that had remained from the age of ignorance (Jahiliyyah) and were still spreading over people's hearts. The people were simple-minded and free from those beliefs, but they were being led along that path by misguided and self-deluded leadership, and the superstitions of the age of ignorance were presented to them as religion.

Surah 72, verse 6, from Sayyid Qutb's Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation):

﴿And that there were men among mankind who used to seek refuge with men among the jinn, so they increased them in rebelliousness.﴾ (72:6) This points to what was well known in the Age of Ignorance (jahiliyyah), and what is still well known in many societies today: that the jinn have authority over the earth and over humans, that they are able to benefit or harm people, that in certain lands, seas and the air these jinn are subjugated, and that their chieftains rule over them. Accordingly, when such people went to an uninhabited place, or were in a forest or mountain, they would seek refuge with the chief jinn of that area, lest its mighty jinn harm them. Having sought this refuge, they would spend the night there.

Satan has been given the power to influence the hearts of humans (except for those who hold firmly to the rope of Allah; such people remain beyond his reach), but whoever among mankind inclines towards Satan, he gives him no benefit, because Satan is the enemy of mankind. In reality he leads man astray and causes him torment. Thus this group of jinn describes this reality in this way.

﴿And that there were men among mankind who used to seek refuge with men among the jinn, so they increased them in turmoil.﴾ (72:6) Here, ruhq (rahaq) means misguidance, anxiety and bewilderment, and it arises in the hearts of those who bow before their enemy and rely upon him, and who do not rely upon Allah nor seek refuge in Allah. The people of Quraysh used to do exactly this, although from the time of Adam (peace be upon him) onward all humans had been commanded: Satan is your enemy.

When the human heart seeks refuge with other than Allah, hoping for benefit from it, or hoping that it will remove harm, such a person finds nothing but anxiety, bewilderment, instability and restlessness. This is the worst form of ruhq: a restlessness in which the heart finds no peace or security.

Everything other than Allah is changeable, perishable, and destined for annihilation. When a heart becomes attached to something other than Allah, it keeps wavering and remains bewildered and confused, and because the thing to which it is attached turns this way and that, its own direction also turns accordingly. Allah alone remains; He does not decline, He is Living and does not die, He is Everlasting and does not change. Therefore whoever attaches himself to Allah attaches himself, as it were, to a fixed axis, and a kind of steadfastness comes into being within him as well.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 72, verse 7:

وانھم ................ احدا (27 : 7) "And that they [humans] also thought, as you thought, that Allah would never send anyone as a messenger." The speech here is addressed to the jinn: just as some humans used to seek refuge with the jinn, so they too held this assumption, just as you hold the assumption that Allah would not send a messenger. But see, Allah did send a messenger, and He has given the messenger this Qur'an, which is providing the means of guidance and right direction. Or the meaning is that their beliefs were as yours are, that Allah would not raise anyone on the Day of Resurrection; therefore they made no preparation for the Hereafter, and paid no heed to the consequence about which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had warned them, because they thought that Allah would not raise anyone.

Both of these assumptions were not in accordance with reality. They were based on ignorance, and on unawareness of the wisdom and design of this entire universe. Allah created all creation in such a way that within it there is the capacity for good as well as the capacity for evil. (As this surah makes clear, the jinn too have been given a dual capacity: for good as well as for evil. However, some of them made themselves embodiments of evil, such as Iblis, who deprived himself of the mercy of Allah and became pure evil.) Allah, the Exalted, assisted goodness by sending messengers. It became the mission of the messengers to awaken the capacity for good found within humans and to polish the good potential that is in their nature. Therefore, the belief that Allah would not send messengers is entirely false.

This is so when by "ba'th" in the verse we take the meaning "the sending of messengers." If by "ba'th" is meant raising up in the Hereafter, then even so this idea is contrary to the wisdom of creation, because we see that the reckoning of human good and evil is not completed in this world. Therefore, according to the wisdom of Allah's creation and the demands of justice, it is also necessary that there be a place where the oppressed are dealt with justly, the righteous are rewarded, the wrongdoers are punished, and the reckoning is conducted fully. And each person should go to the abode that suits his or her life in this world. Therefore there is no place or occasion for the idea that Allah will not raise anyone again. This belief is contrary to divine wisdom and contrary to the principles of justice and fairness.

Thus, in this manner, the jinn sought to correct the mistaken notions of their people, and the Qur'an related this so that the polytheists of Arabia might reflect: even the jinn are re-examining their own assumptions, so what are you doing?

The effects of this final messengership have spread over the entire universe; the natural forces around the cosmos have also changed. Administrative changes have come about in the heavens and the earth, so that they abandon all their activities that are not in agreement with this final messengership, abandon every claim to knowledge of the unseen, and declare that they possess no power whatsoever in this universe.

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 72, verses 8–9:

"And that we had touched the heaven, but found it filled with strong guards and flaming meteors. And that we used to sit there in some of its positions to listen; but whoever listens now finds a flaming meteor lying in wait for him. ..." [This Qur'anic passage is quoted in the original; the Urdu commentary begins below.]

These events, which the Qur'an relates through the jinn, show that in the period before this final message, in which there was no messenger, that is, in the era after Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him), it was the practice of the jinn to go up toward the higher realm (ʿalam-i bala, the realm above). In that higher realm, they would hear the decrees that had been issued regarding this earth and the universe, or that were discussed among the angels. For example, the commands that Allah issued to the angels for execution: these jinn, by reaching certain positions in the higher realm, would overhear them. Then, mixing many falsehoods with these true pieces of information, they would pass them on to soothsayers (kahin), augurs (qiyafa-dan), and other religious leaders in the world. These people would then mix this genuine information with the admixture of the satans and with items serving their own interests, spread it among the people, misguide them, and in this way the satanic plan would continue. How this system functioned between the time of Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) and the Prophet (ﷺ) is not detailed in the Qur'an, and there is no need to learn these details.

Accordingly, this group of jinn says that now it is no longer possible to overhear from the higher realm. When they attempt what they call "lams-i sama" (touching the heaven), they see that strict guards are posted everywhere, and whichever jinn goes above a certain limit is met from the front with a bombardment of shooting stars. Whoever makes such an attempt is destroyed when a meteor falls upon him. They declare that they do not know the unseen, nor what the purposes of these new arrangements are, or what Allah intends:

﴿And that we did not know whether evil is intended for those on the earth, or whether their Lord intends to guide them to right conduct.﴾ (72:10)

All these unseen matters are left to the knowledge of Allah alone. The jinn say that they do not know what the hidden decree will bring forth: whether a calamity is coming upon mankind and they will go further into misguidance, or whether the doors of guidance and mercy have been opened for them. They mentioned guidance alongside evil, as though the true news is only guidance.

When the very source that the soothsayers (kahin) claimed to draw their supposed ideas from is itself denied, what remains of the soothsayers' claims? The jinn have said that they do not know the unseen. Therefore the matter is settled: every kind of false pretension is exposed, and the claims of soothsayers and fortune-tellers ('arrafun) lose all credibility. It is established that only Allah knows the unseen. Hence no one can claim knowledge of the unseen, nor can anyone make prophecies. In this way the Qur'an has purified human reason from every kind of superstition and myth, and closed the doors to all the fabrications that could have been made. It has declared that human reason has now reached maturity (rushd), and that there is no room for superstition and myth in human thought.

How these guardians of the heavens stand, how they restrain the devils, and how shooting stars (shihab thaqib) are launched: concerning this, the Qur'an has not told us anything, nor are there details in authentic hadith. If the Qur'an and Sunnah considered it necessary for humans to know this, and if there were any benefit for them in it, they would certainly have explained it. Since Allah has not told us, this effort is in vain. It cannot add any constructive benefit to our lives or our knowledge.

There is also no need for dispute or debate about shooting stars. These meteors actually move according to the system of this universe. They were like this before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent, and they are the same after him as well. Their mode of operation is the same thing that scientists are now trying to discover, whose thinking sometimes proves correct and sometimes proves wrong and is revised. Even if the present theories of scientists were correct, that would not negate the Qur'an's statement. This is not our subject. It is possible that these meteors are missiles against the devils, and that this act is in accordance with Allah's majesty, of which we do not yet have full knowledge.

As for those who think that this is an allegory, in which it is stated that there can be no falsehood in the word of Allah and that falsehood cannot be mixed into it, and that this verse cannot be taken in its apparent meaning, the state of these unfortunate people is this: they first come to the Qur'an having firmly believed in scientific theories, and their minds are shaped by modern scientific theories. Then they sit down to interpret the Qur'an according to these supposed theories. That is why such people describe the angels as a representation of the forces of good and obedient forces, describe the devils as a representation of the forces of evil and corrupting forces, and describe the shooting stars as an allegory for the memorization of the Qur'an. This is because they cannot understand how something could exist beyond the reach of observation, so that they could witness the existence of angels, jinn and devils in the same way that they see humans and other physical bodies. Therefore they deny these unseen bodies and beings. But if they are asked what the reality is of those supposed notions by which they test the Qur'an and Sunnah, they have no answer.

The truth is that the correct method for interpreting the Qur'an and for forming and explaining the Islamic worldview is that a person should first remove from his mind all prior ideas and conceptions, and study the Qur'an without any prior bias. These prior notions, whether rational, conscious or psychological, should be set aside. Then he should form his ideas and concepts in accordance with the Qur'an, in the light of the realities of this universe and within the bounds of the Prophet's Sunnah. It must not be that the Qur'an and Sunnah are placed in the dock of external ideas and theories and judged by them. We must not deny anything that the Qur'an establishes, nor distort it with interpretations, nor regard as certain those matters which the Qur'an denies. Yes, outside the realm of the clear text of the Qur'an and Sunnah and established realities, a person is free to form whatever theories he wishes through his rational and scientific effort.

We are saying this about the Qur'an in view of the general approach of the people of faith, who interpret the texts of the Qur'an according to their own mental ideas, because they want to see this world in accordance with their own ideas. I cannot absolve myself from this approach. In the early parts of Zilal al-Quran, I too may have unconsciously leaned in this direction. But if the grace of Allah remains with me, I will correct this tendency in future editions. What I am saying here is the truth, and it is a special favour and guidance from Allah to me.

As for those who do not believe in the Qur'an at all, and who stubbornly deny these realities, and who adopt such an attitude merely because they have not yet comprehended them, the conduct of such people is ridiculous. Because science has still not fully comprehended even those realities that are before it. Science is still experimenting on these realities. Therefore, the failure to comprehend these realities does not prove that they do not exist. Moreover, genuine scientists have begun to acknowledge the Lord of the worlds, who is unknown, just as the people of religion do. If they do not accept something in the manner of revealed books, they also do not deny anything. This is because through scientific experiments they have discovered that humanity actually stands at the threshold of a vast world of the unseen (alam al-ghayb). Whereas some time ago they thought they had discovered all realities. Thus scientists have now also begun to express their own limitations of knowledge. Their approach is no longer like that of those self-proclaimed scientific authorities who used to deny celestial realities and unknown realities as a matter of fashion.

The truth is that in this vast and wide universe spread around us there are heaps of unknown realities and secrets. Within this universe there are boundless forces, and this surah shows us a part of this universe. Thus, by accepting these unknown realities, we can hold correct and balanced conceptions about this universe in our minds. In this way, our thinking about the material forces of this world, the spiritual beings, souls, animals, the realities of our physical environment, our life, our self and our actions becomes correct. This balanced thinking is what distinguishes a Muslim, refining him well in comparison with other people. He neither accepts superstitions and myths, nor claims that he has mastered all the realities of this universe. And the source of this balanced thinking is the Qur'an and Sunnah. Thus a Muslim tests his thinking on the touchstone of the Qur'an and Sunnah, and measures all realities according to the Qur'an and Sunnah, whether they are moral realities or physical ones.

For descending into the fields of the unknown and for the ventures of human reason, there are defined paths. Islam advances human reason to enter these fields. But beyond these defined paths and fields there are also realms that reason has no power to reach. These fields lie beyond reason. Moreover, human reason does not need to reach those realms, because the duty that the Creator has assigned to humans on this earth, and for which humans were created, namely that of humanity as Allah's vicegerent on earth (khalifat Allah fil-ard), from this perspective humans do not need to know about those unknown realms. This is because Allah has given humans through the Qur'an and Sunnah the knowledge they needed, so that they may know their place, status and environment in this world and on this earth. Acquiring those sciences is not within human power, and the unseen matters, namely the angels, jinn and devils, all fall into this category. Likewise, the human soul, the creation of man and his end fall within this domain. These are fields where human reason can rely only on revelation.

As for those who walk in the light of the guidance of Allah's Sunnah, they stop at the boundaries of these fields which Allah and His Messenger have shown to humans. Allah and the Messenger (ﷺ) have given humans the awareness regarding these hidden realms, that they should believe that Allah is very great and that He is the Most Wise, and what the station of humans in this world is, and what their status is. In this regard, humans have been advised to reflect within the sphere of their reach, within their environment, and to act as much as is within their power. And within the limits of their strength, they should employ whatever technology they discover for increasing production and providing facilities for life in this world, and fulfil their duties here as Allah's deputies. They should work in accordance with Allah's instructions, turn their face towards Allah and advance, rising to the height that Allah has chosen for them.

As for those who do not accept Allah's guidance, they exist in two major groups. One group uses only the weapon of their reason to discover the reality of Allah, although human reason is limited and the Divine Being is unlimited. This group seeks to know the unseen realities not in the light of the revealed books, but through the strength of their reason. This group is the philosophers, who have given a rational explanation of this universe and its relationships. The example of these people is like children who set out to climb the summit of a great mountain whose height they do not even know, and who advance stumbling and falling, or like a few children who have not yet learned the alphabet but are trying to discover the existence of this universe. Among these people are counted the great philosophers of Greece, and also those philosophers and logicians among Muslims who have thought along the lines of the Greek philosophers. And among this category also come those modern philosophers who do not think along Islamic lines. This is one group.

The second group is the one that has despaired of this way of thinking. This group has restricted itself to knowledge based on experience, and this class ignores all unknown matters. In their scientific world there is no path to reach those fields, and in this regard this class is also not ready to take guidance from the Qur'an and Sunnah. This class is not prepared to accept the guidance of Allah and His Messenger because it thinks that an experiential perception of God is impossible for humans. This class dominated the intellectual world of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. But from the beginning of the twentieth century, this class came to know that its scientific arrogance is also based on ignorance. This is because the people of this class, while carrying out experimental work on this matter, reached the conclusion that this matter is in fact close to a light and radiance, and they have still not been able to comprehend the reality of light and radiance. And the law of light and its reality also actually lie beyond the human sphere of perception. Therefore the physical scientists of the twentieth century have also come to a fair understanding of their own narrowness of vision.

After this, the jinn describe, in relation to Allah's guidance, their own condition and position: that they too, just like humans, possess the capacity for guidance and misguidance, and are a responsible creation like humans. Here they state their belief concerning the Lord, the Exalted: that this is the faith we have embraced, and they clearly present their view of guidance and misguidance.

وانا منا .................... ذلک (72 : 11)

﴿And among us there are the righteous, and among us there are those who are otherwise than that.﴾

كنا طرائق قددا (72 : 11)

﴿We were of divergent ways.﴾

The passage opens mid-verse, with the Qur'anic quotation partly cut off in the source. Translating the text as given:

and that we thought that we could never frustrate Allah in the earth, nor could we escape Him by flight" (27:21)... "And that we thought that we could never frustrate Allah in the earth, nor could we escape Him by flight."

This was their belief: that Allah has complete power over them on this earth. They also held the belief that they could not escape from Allah. These were the jinn, among whom some people sought refuge in the Age of Ignorance. Yet these jinn confess their own helplessness and Allah's power. They speak of their own weakness and of Allah's authority. They hold the belief in their own powerlessness and in Allah's being the Subduer and the Compeller. They say this not only to their own people but also tell the polytheists of Makkah that true power belongs to Allah alone, who holds this universe together.

And now, after hearing and understanding the message of guidance, they say:

﴿And that when we heard the guidance, we believed in it. So whoever believes in his Lord will have no fear of any loss or injustice (that is, of being given work beyond his capacity)﴾ (72:13, cf. 27:31 quoted here as "وانا لما... امنا به"). This is the duty of every person who hears the message of guidance. These people call the Qur'an here by the name of guidance, because the true nature of the Qur'an is guidance and its result is also guidance... and they have complete trust in their Lord, as every believer should have in his Master.

﴿So whoever believes in his Lord will have no fear of any loss or injustice (that is, of being given work beyond his capacity)﴾ (27:31). After faith, a believer begins to place full trust in Allah. He has full confidence in the justice of Allah, and this is the reality of faith: that Allah is just. He does not usurp the right of any believer. He does not oppress anyone. Nor does He burden anyone beyond his capacity. Allah does not deprive a believing servant of his due even by a particle's weight. And Allah protects His servant from rahq as well. Rahq means subjecting someone to labour and hardship beyond his strength. Therefore no other person will dare to oppress a believer, because the believer is under Allah's watch. It is true that a believer sometimes lacks the comforts of this world, but such deprivations do not fall under the meaning of "nahs" (misfortune). Sometimes a believer is also subjected to torments, and these come from some minor powers of this earth. But these torments do not fall within the meaning of rahq, because Allah knows who can bear how much hardship and who is fit for how much ease. And Allah brings some servants closer to Himself by putting them into hardships, and these are beneficial for them.

Therefore a believer is, psychologically speaking, protected from injustice and from being burdened beyond his endurance. Hence he should be: ﴿so he should not fear any injustice, nor think that a burden beyond his capacity has been placed upon him﴾ (27:31). This conception creates contentment, ease and tranquillity within a person. A person does not feel anxiety, sting or restlessness. Even if he is in hardship, he does not lament or panic, does not fear, and does not close doors upon himself. He regards hardship as a trial, shows patience, and hopes from Allah for abundance. And for this too he receives a reward. Thus, in both states, of wealth and poverty, and of weakness and strength, he remains in profit, and he suffers no loss.

And this group of jinn impressed this truth in a very excellent manner. After this, they now make clear the reality of guidance and misguidance, and mention reward and punishment for guidance and misguidance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 72, verse 14:

"And that among us are the Muslims (those who submit to Allah), and among us are those who deviate from the truth. So whoever has embraced Islam (the path of submission), they have sought out the way of salvation; but as for those who deviate from the truth, they will become fuel for Hell."

Qasit means one who is unjust, and one who turns aside from the truth, departing from justice and righteousness. The jinn have mentioned it in opposition to the Muslims, and there is a subtle indication in this: that a Muslim is just and a reformer, while his opposing party is unjust and corrupt.

﴿Fa man aslama ... tahharraw rashada﴾ (72:14): "Whoever has embraced Islam (the path of submission), they have sought out the way of salvation." Here their act is expressed by the word "tahharaw", meaning to seek the path of guidance with very deep reflection. Its opposite is misguidance and error. Taharri means to adopt the right path with great care, thinking well and investigating thoroughly. It does not mean going wherever one's face turns, without thought or consideration. That is, upon accepting Islam they reached the right path. The indication here is that Islam is the very path of salvation, and this is a very beautiful indication.

"As for those who deviate from the truth, they shall be fuel for Hell." That is, the decision regarding their being people of Hell has been made, and when they are cast into Hell, the fire of Hell will blaze fiercely because of them, just as a fire blazes more intensely when fed with dry fuel.

From this it is also understood that jinn too will be subjected to the punishment of Hell. And it is also established that righteous jinn will be entitled to Paradise. This is the reality, and it is not permissible for any person to adopt belief in anything other than this. If anyone does so, it will be false, and what the Qur'an says will be correct beyond any dispute. Therefore, what is true of the jinn will also be the end of mankind.

Up to this point, the Qur'an has related the words of the jinn in their own expressions. But now, from the Divine side, a summary of their statements is presented, that they also say that every creature that adopts the path of steadfastness, Allah will treat it in the same way.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 72, verses 16–17:

وان .................................... صعد

Allah says: those jinn who used to say about Us that if people, or unjust and disbelieving people, were to walk upon the right path, We would surely give them abundant water to drink, and thus their provision would increase, so that "We" might test them as to whether they give thanks or are ungrateful.

The change in style, whereby instead of quoting the words of the jinn, their statement is rendered in Qur'anic words, and such a manner of speech about the jinn occurs at several places in the Qur'an, is intended to create further emphasis in the speech, and the reader pays closer attention.

In this notice that draws attention, there are several realities, in accordance with which the faith of a believer is formed, and in accordance with them he makes decisions in affairs and determines the interrelations of events.

The first reality is how nations, societies and communities can remain upon the straight path and reach Allah. Then, what is the connection between arriving at Allah, the increase of production, and the attainment of prosperity, while the primary cause of prosperity is the arrangement and abundance of irrigation? As for life, it is indeed formed from water. Even in our present industrial age, prosperity still depends upon water and irrigation, although life has not remained dependent upon agriculture alone. Yet development and progress still revolve around water.

The truth is that if a people remain upon the right path, not only do they become developed and prosperous, but such people also attain supreme authority on earth: the Arab nation.

A clear example of this is that in the Days of Ignorance, the Arabs of the Arabian Peninsula lived a most backward life. But when they walked upon the right path, the doors of such lands opened for them where water was available in great quantity. And when these same Arabs became deeds-wise corrupt and deviated from the right path, they again became backward, and therefore they are in a state of misery at this time. And they will remain in misery until they return to the right path. And whenever they return, prosperity will come upon them and they will be granted establishment on earth.

If there exist nations that are not upon the right path but are still abundant in resources, then Allah will impose upon them other punishments, and they will be afflicted with many calamities and tribulations. Such nations will fall in terms of humanity, values, human dignity and nobility. Thus their prosperity and material progress will become meaningless, and their life will be bitter and laborious. Such nations will be deprived of human honour, and there will be no tranquillity in their lives. We have explained this theme in the commentary on Surah Nuh.

And the second reality that becomes apparent from this notice is that prosperity and establishment on earth are in fact also a trial, a test. Allah tests human beings through good and bad circumstances. The truth is that giving thanks to Allah in prosperity is a much more difficult task than enduring patiently in adversity, because in ordinary observation a person's attention becomes diverted to one side, and his defensive faculties are gathered together, and he devotes all his powers to resisting the situation. For example, he remembers Allah, prays to Allah, and seeks help from Allah in those difficult circumstances when all worldly supports have ended, and then a person takes the support of Allah. As for prosperity, it makes a person heedless; a person becomes occupied with trivialities. Human limbs become lax, the power of resistance falls asleep, and causes of heedlessness and straying are made available to a person, and a person very easily becomes entangled in the snare of Satan.

When a person is tested with prosperity and an abundance of blessings, he needs to remain alert at all times. Wealth and property often afflict a person with rebellion. A person does not give thanks to Allah, becomes miserly in spending in the way of Allah, and begins to be extravagant in worldly expenses. These two things become a punishment for the balance of life. Likewise, the power of authority also often blinds a person; he becomes oppressive and rebellious, he encroaches upon the rights of others, and goes beyond limits. After oppressing people, such a person then encroaches upon the rights of Allah. Likewise, the trials of wealth and beauty lead a person into arrogance, pride, straying, evil deeds, wicked conduct, and immorality. Similarly, if someone is intelligent and clever, he considers others contemptible, becomes self-deceived, and tramples upon lofty values. In short, every blessing is a trial, unless someone remembers Allah in time and seeks Allah's refuge.

The third reality is that as a consequence of turning away from the remembrance of Allah, on one hand a person is tested in prosperity, and on the other hand he will also be afflicted with the punishment of the Hereafter. The Qur'an explicitly states this:

﴿يَسْلُكْهُ عَذَابًا صَعَدًا﴾ (72:17) "His Lord will make him enter a severe punishment." That is, this punishment will be very intense, just as a man climbing an ascent finds it difficult. The more he climbs, the more difficult his pace becomes. The Qur'an has, at several places, expressed the intensity of punishment in terms of climbing an ascent. At another place it says:

﴿فَمَن يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَن يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ وَمَن يُرِدْ أَن يُضِلَّهُ يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقًا حَرَجًا كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِي السَّمَاءِ﴾ (6:125) "So whomever Allah intends to guide, He expands his breast for Islam, and whomever He intends to lead astray, He makes his breast constricted and tight, as if he were climbing up into the sky."

And at another place it says:

﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُودًا﴾ (74:17) "I shall soon impose upon him a grievous ascent."

It is possible that this third verse is a narration of the words of the jinn, and it is also possible that it is the words of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 72, verse 19:

وانہ ........................ لبدا

"That is, they all gathered together and formed a massed body, ready to attack him at the time when he stood to call upon Allah, that is, to perform prayer before Allah. Salah (prayer) in its original meaning signifies supplication (du'a). If this verse is the statement of the jinn, then it is a report from Allah of their words: that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood for prayer and recited, the polytheists of Makkah would gather around him, as is mentioned in Surah al-Ma'arij:

فمال .................... عزین (73) (07 : 63۔ 73)

"So what is the matter with those who disbelieve, that they rush toward you from the right and from the left, in separate groups?" [70:36-37]

They would listen to the Qur'an in utter astonishment and would not accept it; or they would gather from every side to attack him. But Allah protected him from them, and such occasions occurred many times. If this is the statement of the jinn, then they are expressing their amazement at the attitude of the polytheists of Makkah before their own people. And if it is taken as the word of Allah from the beginning, then they are listening to the speech, marvelling, and these people are gathering around the Messenger of Allah in the way that the woolen threads of a woven cloth are tightly joined to one another. This meaning is more fitting to the wonder, astonishment and awe that remained present throughout the whole speech of the jinn, for the entire speech of the jinn is in fact a model of expressions of wonder and amazement. And Allah knows best!

When the speech of the jinn concerning the Islamic call and the Qur'an comes to an end here, in which they expressed their wonder, in which their awareness and thinking were stirred, and they saw that the earth and the heavens, the jinn and the angels, and the stars and planets were all in motion in relation to this great call and this great speech, this magnificent order of the universe was also affected by it, and this is a most important and serious movement. Then, with this, the address now turns to the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is given very clear, decisive and firm instructions that he should devote himself wholly to the propagation (of the message), and that he should declare that he is not the master of anyone's benefit or harm, nor do I claim knowledge of the unseen, nor can I change the destiny of people. This is said with great seriousness and in a tone of reproach, with great firmness and in a decisive manner:

Say (O Muhammad): "Indeed, I only call upon my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with Him."

﴿Say: "Indeed, I only call upon my Lord, and I associate none with Him"﴾ (72:20). This declaration comes at the time when the jinn also declare this before their people.

﴿And we will never associate anyone with our Lord﴾ (72:2). Thus this declaration will have a great effect. This declaration will simultaneously become the declaration of both jinn and humans, and it will be the identity of both. Whoever disassociates himself from this declaration will, as it were, separate himself from both jinn and humans. He will be distant from both worlds and both communities.

﴿Say: "Indeed, I do not control for you any harm or any benefit"﴾ (72:21). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is commanded to devote himself purely to Allah, to renounce every kind of claim, and to declare clearly that no attribute of Allah's attributes belongs to him, but rather that he is a servant and does not set up any partner with Allah. It is Allah alone who holds the power of benefit and harm over humankind. Here the Qur'an places right guidance (rushd) in opposition to harm (darar), and this is the same point the jinn had made.

﴿And that we do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth, or whether their Lord intends to guide them to right conduct﴾ (72:10). Thus a correspondence arises between the two verses and the two statements, both in words and in meaning, and this correspondence is intended both in the narrative and in the commentary upon it.

Here the Noble Qur'an also negates, even regarding the jinn, that they can give benefit or harm to anyone, and it is also refuted regarding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he can give benefit or harm to anyone; giving benefit and harm is established as a characteristic of Allah. Thus the Islamic creed and the Islamic worldview emerge clear and pure.

Say, "No one can protect me from Allah, nor can I find any refuge apart from Him. My only task is to deliver the messages of Allah and His word." (72:22–23)

This is a most terrifying warning. From it we learn how delicate and serious the matter of prophethood is. Prophethood and the call to Islam are extremely sensitive matters. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself is commanded to declare that no one can save him from the grip of Allah, that there is no refuge other than Allah, and that the only way to be safe is to convey what has been entrusted to him from Allah. This is the one matter for which a guarantee has been given. In this matter he has no discretion. He is only charged with conveying the message, and there is no other course open to him. For this is a compulsory service, and he cannot flee from it or find any place to hide. For him there is only one option: to keep performing his duty.

Consider how delicate, serious and frightening the matter of prophethood and the call is. It is not a voluntary affair, where one may present the call if he wishes and leave it if he does not. It is a compulsory service and a most sensitive duty. Allah is watching, and no one can escape from Allah. Nor is it a personal pastime or hobby, pursued for personal pleasure or the enjoyment of gratification. It is the command of the absolute Sovereign, from which one cannot turn away, and about which one cannot hesitate. Thus the nature of the Islamic call becomes clear: those who come after the Messenger as callers should again understand its status, that it is a compulsory obligation and a most sensitive and serious matter, and that Allah, the Great and Exalted, Himself supervises it.

(72:23–24) "Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, for him is the fire of Hell, and they will abide therein forever. (They will not desist from their course) until, when they see what they are promised, they will know who is weaker in helpers and fewer in number."

This is a terrifying threat and warning, both overt and implicit, for those people to whom this message reaches and who turn away from it, especially since they had already been sternly warned that whoever accepts and then does not convey it to others.

If the polytheists take pride in their strength and large numbers, and they compare themselves with Muhammad ﷺ and the Companions, whose strength is weak and whose number is small, then they will soon come to know the measure of their strength when they see with their own eyes the scene with which they are being warned, whether in this world or in the Hereafter, that:

"Who is weaker in helpers and fewer in number." Who is feeble, powerless and without dignity, and who is mighty and strong.

This is a terrifying threat and warning, both overt and implicit, for those people to whom this message reaches and who turn away from it, especially since they had already been sternly warned that whoever accepts and then does not convey it to others.

"Who is weaker in helpers and fewer in number." Who is feeble, powerless and without dignity, and who is mighty and strong.

Now look back at what the jinn said: "And we thought that we could never cause Allah to fail on earth, nor could we escape Him by flight." The Prophet ﷺ is now commanded to deny, in addition to power, any knowledge of the unseen concerning himself.

Say: "I do not know whether that which you are promised is near, or whether my Lord will appoint for it a long term" (Qur'an 72:25). In matters of the call, you have no authority, and you have no personal right in it. Your duty is only to convey the message, and by doing so you enter the secure enclosure. Only the one who fulfils the right of conveying the message can enter that secure enclosure. And the evil end with which Allah warns against denial and disobedience is also within Allah's authority. You have no real authority over it either. Nor do you know its appointed time of occurrence, whether it is near or far. These are all matters of the unseen, and no one knows their knowledge except Allah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ knows nothing of it. Knowledge of these matters is specific to Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 72, verse 26:

﴿He is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone﴾ (72:26-27). Thus the attributes of divinity are negated from the Prophet ﷺ, and he remains only a chosen servant (bandah mukhtar). For a human being there can be no quality or honour greater than servitude (bandagi). Servitude and worship (ubudiyyah) are the highest rank and degree among the stations of man. In this way, the Prophet ﷺ is freed from all the attributes of divinity, and he is commanded to convey the message: ﴿Say: I do not know whether that which you are promised is near, or whether my Lord will appoint for it a long duration. He is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone﴾ (72:25-26).

There is only one exception to this: that Allah grants permission regarding some unseen matter and informs a Messenger of it. And this too concerns those matters which relate to the duties of calling people to the faith, because the matters revealed to the Prophet ﷺ were also unseen matters. At his time, commands were revealed to the Messenger ﷺ according to a measure, and the Messengers were also watched from before and behind, to see whether they had conveyed the unseen that had come to them. The Messenger ﷺ is commanded to proclaim this matter as well, and to do so with complete clarity, seriousness, and deep humility (khushu').

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 72, verses 27–28:

Except for a Messenger whom He has chosen (for imparting the knowledge of the unseen), then He sends before him and behind him guards, so that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord, and He encompasses all that is with them, and He has numbered everything in count. (72:27–28)

Thus, the Messengers whom Allah chooses for conveying His call, Allah reveals to them some aspects of His knowledge of the unseen, and those aspects are what is contained in the revelation. That is, the subjects of the revelation, its method, namely the angels who bring the revelation, and the source from which they bring it, namely the Preserved Tablet (Lawh Mahfuz) and its system of protection, which is mentioned, and the other matters connected with the Messenger's prophethood and call. All these matters are unseen matters, and none among mankind knows about them. (Therefore, the unseen that is given to the Messenger relates to divine revelation.)

And alongside this, guardians appointed by Allah are set around the Messengers. These guardians both protect them and watch over their work. These guardians save them from the whisperings of Satan, save them from the interferences of the devils, and save them from the desires and wishes of Satan. They save them from those human weaknesses that would cause them to be slack in prophethood and call, to forget any matter, or to deviate from the right path, and they save them from other human faults and frailties.

However, within this protective system for the prophets there is a kind of fear and sensitivity. Consider the manner of expression.

"Fa-innahu yasluku..." (72:27): "then He sends before him and behind him guards." So every Messenger is under constant observation, to see whether he is discharging his duty or not.

"Li-ya'lama..." (72:28): "so that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord." Allah already knows, but Allah wills that the act of conveying should actually proceed from them and become manifest, and that His knowledge be related to it.

"Wa-ahata bima ladayhim" (72:28): "and He encompasses all that is with them." Their souls, their lives, whatever they are, and whatever is in their surroundings, Allah knows. Nothing is hidden from the knowledge of Allah.

"Wa-ahsa kulla shay'in 'adada" (72:28): "and He has numbered everything in count." Not only what relates to the Messengers, but His encompassing and counting includes everything, down to the smallest particle.

Just imagine this state! A Messenger is conveying the message, and guards are behind and before him. They are both protectors and watchers, and Allah maintains direct contact with the entire environment of the Messengers. Therefore, the duty of the Messenger and his service is a compulsory, military-like service, and he has to discharge this duty. The Messenger is doing his work; he is not autonomous, he cannot show weakness, nor can he follow his own desires, nor can he go after his own preferences. Rather, it is an extremely sensitive, serious and strict duty under observation. Every Messenger knows this and thus continues discharging his duty, and does not look here and there, because he knows that he is under strict observation. He knows that every one of his actions is within Allah's knowledge and is open before Him.

This is a scene which, on seeing it, creates in the heart of every person a deep sympathy for the Messenger, and along with sympathy there also grips him a fear and awe, that the matter of the call to the religion is extremely sensitive.

This surah concludes with this awe-inspiring and overwhelming guidance, and it began with the same kind of atmosphere, which was introduced with the lengthy account of the jinn and in which the trembling events of the jinn were described.

This surah, whose verses number no more than 12 (sic), establishes countless facts related to the Islamic worldview, and proposes a very balanced and straight path of Islamic belief and the Islamic worldview, within which there is no exaggeration, nor excess nor deficiency. This surah also gives a very moderate line regarding the unseen world. It neither closes the doors of the unseen to mankind, nor permits mankind to fabricate fables and superstitions about the unseen world. And the comment of the jinn in this surah is extremely precious.
